issues.detail: The Greek pronoun 'αυτω' (autō) refers to 'him' (a person), but the Vietnamese translation uses 'nó' (it), which changes the subject from a person to an object/thing.

The Greek text says 'εδοθη αυτω εξουσια' (he was given authority), but the Vietnamese translation adds the word 'quyền' (power/right) twice, once for the war and once for the authority, whereas the Greek only uses 'exousia' for the latter part.
